claims.text: Chemical short-range-order clusters form during solidification of the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy.
The short-range-order clusters act as dynamic obstacles that pin dislocations.
Low temperatures and high strain rates preserve the stability and pinning effectiveness of the short-range-order clusters.
Strong short-range-order pinning at low temperatures or high strain rates increases yield strength.
Strong short-range-order pinning at low temperatures or high strain rates increases strain hardening.
At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, thermal activation causes short-range-order clusters to reconfigure or partially dissolve.
Thermally induced weakening of short-range order reduces its dislocation-pinning efficacy and promotes dynamic recovery.
The increased dynamic recovery at elevated temperature or lower strain rate enhances ductility.
The as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn material is a single-phase solid solution containing nanoscale fluctuations in chemical ordering.
High-temperature pre-annealing disrupts short-range order without changing the overall single-phase nature of the alloy.
At low temperatures and high strain rates, as-solidified specimens will have higher yield strength than pre-annealed, short-range-order-disrupted specimens.
At low temperatures and high strain rates, as-solidified specimens will exhibit more pronounced strain hardening than pre-annealed specimens.
At elevated temperatures or low strain rates, mechanical-response differences between as-solidified and pre-annealed specimens will diminish.
The critical temperature for short-range-order stability or dissolution is likely near 600–700 K.
The proposed mechanism applies when dislocation dynamics dominate rather than full diffusion control or phase transformations.
At extreme temperatures or very high or low strain rates, mechanisms other than short-range-order-controlled dislocation pinning may become significant.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is obtained from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi by omitting Co.
